mainTopic: The יבמה's status and כתובה after יבום, and how שמעון בן שטח shaped the כתובה
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a יבם who marries his dead brother's wife. First the גמרא proves from the פסוק 'ולקחה לו לאשה' that after יבום she is fully his wife, so the איסור of אשת אח never comes back, even after a גט. Her כתובה is paid from the first husband's property, because Heaven gave her to the יבם. If the first husband left nothing, the יבם pays, so that divorcing her is not easy for him. The גמרא then explains the extra lines of the משנה. The word 'וכן' teaches that even a regular wife cannot be limited to money set aside. The words 'if he divorced her' show the law follows רבי אבא. And a remarried יבמה goes back on her first כתובה, even though the יבם never wrote it. Finally, רב יהודה and a ברייתא tell the history of the כתובה. Every early fix left divorce too easy, until שמעון בן שטח ruled that all of the husband's property guarantees the כתובה. The chapter האשה then closes with a הדרן.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to say he can divorce and remarry her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it is not obvious that the יבם can divorce his יבמה and then remarry her. We might have thought that once the מצוה of יבום is done, the old איסור of אשת אח comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he already did the מצוה the Torah put on him, so now the איסור of אשת אח should come back. That is why the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the earlier 'isn't this obvious?' question. It shows there was a reasonable mistake the משנה needed to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבמה was forbidden as אשת אח, and only the מצוה of יבום allowed her. One could argue the permission only covered the מצוה itself, so after a גט the old איסור returns. The משנה's words 'כאשתו לכל דבר' teach that the איסור is gone completely.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to reject)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
The prohibition against marrying a brother's wife
It teaches us (the point the text is making)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether he may divorce her. A גט works for any wife. The real question is whether he may take her back after the גט, or whether she becomes forbidden again as his brother's wife.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the מצוה the Merciful One placed on him, he has done it,
and now she should stand toward him
under the prohibition of a brother's wife,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier 'פשיטא' challenge about why the משנה says 'כאשתו לכל דבר.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken view that the משנה needed to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the מצוה of יבום is done and he divorces her, the איסור of אשת אח comes back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור of אשת אח is gone for good, so he may remarry her after a גט.

steps.title: Maybe the brother's-wife prohibition really does come back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back and asks why the 'mistaken' view is wrong. Maybe the איסור of אשת אח really does return.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say it really is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It asks why we should not accept the idea that the איסור comes back. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 1 sounded logical. So the גמרא asks for a source that rules it out. Without one, the 'mistaken' view might actually be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: And say it really is so (a challenge: why not accept this?)

phrases.english: And say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe after the גט she really does go back to being forbidden as his brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 by asking why the 'mistaken' view is actually wrong.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that the איסור of אשת אח does not return
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'mistaken' view seems logical, so a source is needed to reject it.

steps.title: The פסוק makes her fully his wife
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ולקחה לו לאשה' teaches that once he takes her, she becomes his regular wife. The old איסור of אשת אח no longer applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And he shall take her to him as a wife.' Once he takes her, she becomes like his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק about יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לו לאשה,' meaning 'to him as a wife,' show that יבום turns her into his ordinary wife. Her status is no longer just 'permitted for the מצוה.' So a גט and remarriage work for her the same as for any wife.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall take her to him as a wife
She becomes like his wife

steps.whatToRemember: After יבום, the יבמה is a full regular wife. The איסור of אשת אח is gone for good, so he can divorce her and remarry her.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall take her to him as a wife."
Once he has taken her, she becomes like his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסור of אשת אח might come back after the מצוה is done.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לו לאשה' makes her his regular wife for good.

steps.title: Why her כתובה comes from the first husband's property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception that her כתובה is paid from the first husband's property. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Except that her כתובה is on the property of her first husband.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the משנה and asks why it rules this way. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is fully his wife 'in every way,' we would expect the יבם to owe her a כתובה of his own. The משנה makes an exception here, so the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: Except that / only that
The marriage contract and the money promised to the wife
The property of her first (dead) husband
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Except that her marriage contract shall be
upon the property of her first husband.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'לכל דבר' clause to the משנה's exception about the כתובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the יבם does not write his own כתובה, and her כתובה is paid from the first husband's property instead.

steps.title: Heaven gave her to him
steps.stepSummary: The יבם did not choose this wife. Heaven gave her to him through the מצוה of יבום, so he does not have to write his own כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because Heaven gave him this wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the wife came to him from Heaven, not by his own choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal husband writes a כתובה because he chose to marry this woman. Here the Torah's מצוה brought her to the יבם. So she relies on the כתובה her first husband already owed her.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave him / made him acquire
From Heaven

phrases.english: a wife they granted to him
from Heaven.
phrases.notes: He did not pick her himself. The Torah's מצוה of יבום brought her to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because Heaven gave her to him through the מצוה, he does not owe his own כתובה. Her כתובה rests on the first husband's property.

steps.title: If the first husband left nothing, the יבם pays
steps.stepSummary: If the first husband left no property, the יבמה still gets a כתובה from the יבם. Otherwise it would be too easy for him to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she has nothing from the first husband, she has a כתובה from the second. This is so that she will not be easy in his eyes to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the משנה's rule. The first husband's property comes first, but if there is none, the יבם must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic reason any wife has a כתובה is to make divorce costly, so the husband will not send her away lightly. That reason also applies to the יבם. So when there is no money from the first husband, the יבם becomes responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not have
She has
Light / unimportant in his eyes
To send her away, meaning to divorce her

steps.whatToRemember: Her כתובה comes first from the first husband's property, because Heaven gave her to the יבם. If that property is not there, the יבם pays, so that divorcing her is not easy for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the general reason for a כתובה, protecting the wife from an easy divorce, also applies in יבום. It applies even though the יבם never chose to marry her.

phrases.english: And if she does not have anything from the first husband,

So that she will not be light

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵית לַהּ מֵרִאשׁוֹן, אִית לַהּ מִשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fallback rule to the answer in step 5: when the first husband left nothing, the יבם pays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first husband left no property, the יבם must pay her כתובה, so that divorcing her is not easy for him.

steps.title: Why does the משנה add 'and similarly'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the יבם cannot point to specific money as her כתובה. It asks what the extra word 'וכן' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the יבם may not tell her, 'Here is your כתובה.' What does 'and similarly' come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why the word 'וכן' is there. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the rule that a husband cannot limit the כתובה to specific money is said about a יבם and then repeated with 'וכן' for a regular husband. The rule sounds the same in both cases, so the גמרא wants to know why the משנה had to say it twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here is your כתובה': pointing to specific money set aside for it
'And similarly': the משנה applies the same rule to another case
What? Used to ask what a word means or adds

phrases.english: He may not say to her, "Here is your כתובה."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. He can't set aside one pile of money as her כתובה, because all his property stays backing it.

phrases.english: What does "and similarly" add?
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say 'and similarly' about a regular husband and his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה about how the יבמה's כתובה is backed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needed to apply the rule to a regular husband with 'וכן'.

steps.title: Even a regular wife does not rely on money set aside
steps.stepSummary: Without 'וכן' we might think a regular wife, whose כתובה says 'what I bought and will buy,' is fine with money set aside. The משנה teaches that she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the rule applies only to the יבמה, because the יבם never wrote her the clause 'what I have bought and what I will buy.' But a regular wife has that clause in writing, so maybe she trusts the money set aside for her. The משנה teaches us that this is wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: 'וכן' blocks a mistaken idea about a regular wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה has no written כתובה from the יבם, so of course she needs all his property behind her. A regular wife has a written lien on everything he owns and will own, so we might think she is calm about him setting money aside. The משנה says no: for her too, he cannot limit the כתובה to specific money.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces a mistaken idea the text rejects
'What I have bought and what I will buy': the clause putting all his property behind the כתובה
She feels secure and relies on it
It teaches us: the new point the text is making

phrases.english: You might have said:
It is only there, where he did not write for her
phrases.notes: 'There' means the יבמה. The יבם never wrote her his own כתובה.

phrases.english: "what I have bought and what I will buy,"
but here, where he did write for her
"what I have bought and what I will buy,"
say she relies on it,
phrases.notes: She'd feel secure and accept the money he set aside.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכן' teaches that even a regular wife with a written lien cannot be limited to money set aside.

steps.title: 'If he divorced her' shows the משנה follows רבי אבא
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'if he divorced her,' the גמרא learns that only divorce frees the property, as רבי אבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he divorced her, she has only her כתובה. So if he divorced her, yes; if he did not divorce her, no. This teaches us the law follows רבי אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and draws a lesson from what they leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he divorces her, she just collects her כתובה and the property is no longer tied up. The משנה names divorce on purpose, so without a divorce the property stays tied up. This matches רבי אבא, who said divorce is the only way for him to get full control of the property.

keyTerms.meaning: He divorced her
Yes ... no: the pattern for reading a lesson from exact words
In line with רבי אבא

phrases.english: If he divorced her, she has only her כתובה.
If he divorced her, yes,
if he did not divorce her, no.
It teaches us the law follows רבי אבא.
phrases.notes: רבי אבא is quoted earlier in the sugya. His view is that only divorce lets him take full control of the property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only divorce frees the property from the יבמה's claim, as רבי אבא said.

steps.title: Why say 'if he remarried her' when we already learned it?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a remarried יבמה is like any wife. The גמרא objects that another משנה (תנינא) already taught that a remarried wife goes back on her first כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he remarried her, she is like all women and has only her כתובה. What does that teach us? We already learned: a man who divorces his wife and remarries her takes her back on the terms of the first כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last clause of the משנה and challenges it as unnecessary, since another משנה already says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That other משנה teaches that a remarried wife returns on her first כתובה, so nothing new needs to be written. That seems to cover the remarried יבמה too. So the extra line in our משנה looks repeated, and the גמרא wants to know what new point it makes.

keyTerms.meaning: He remarried her after divorcing her
On the terms of the first כתובה

phrases.english: If he remarried her, she is like all women,
and she has only her כתובה.
"If he remarried her": what does it teach us?
We already learned:
One who divorces a woman and remarries her
remarries her on the terms of the first כתובה!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶחְזִירָה, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the final clause of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about a יבם who remarried the יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה already teaches that a remarried wife returns on her first כתובה, so this clause seems to repeat it.

steps.title: Why the remarried יבמה case is still needed
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought a remarried יבמה needs a new כתובה from the יבם himself, because he never wrote her first one. The משנה teaches that she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a regular wife goes back to her old כתובה because her husband wrote it himself. But his יבמה, whose כתובה he did not write, needs a new one from him if he divorced and remarried her. The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 10. The new rule about the יבמה is not a repeat, because her case has a reason to be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular wife's first כתובה was written by her own husband, so it makes sense that it still covers her after remarriage. A יבמה's כתובה was written by the dead brother, so we might think the יבם must now write his own. The משנה's words 'she is like all women' (הרי היא ככל הנשים) tell us she still goes back to the first כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
His יבמה, his dead brother's widow whom he married
He divorced her and took her back
It teaches us (the point the source comes to make)

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is only his wife, since he himself
wrote her a כתובה from himself,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יְבִמְתּוֹ דְּלָא אִיהוּ כְּתַב לַהּ,
phrases.english: but his יבמה, for whom he did not write it,
where he divorced her and took her back,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case is not repetitive because there was a reasonable mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the יבם never wrote the first כתובה, after divorce and remarriage he must write a new one from his own property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remarried יבמה is like any wife and goes back to her first כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: A remarried יבמה goes back to the original כתובה, even though the יבם did not write it.

steps.title: How שמעון בן שטח fixed the כתובה system
steps.stepSummary: At first the כתובה sums of two hundred and one hundred had to be set aside. Men grew old without marrying, until שמעון בן שטח ruled that all a man's property backs the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: At first they wrote two hundred for a virgin and a מנה for a widow. Men grew old and did not marry, until שמעון בן שטח came and made a rule that all of a man's property is a guarantee for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, the history behind the rule that the husband's property backs the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old system set the כתובה money aside ahead of time, and this kept men from getting married. שמעון בן שטח's fix was that no money has to be set aside. Instead, all of the husband's property is held as a guarantee to pay it. This ties back to the earlier steps, where money set aside for the כתובה was not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, in earlier times
A מנה, one hundred זוז
He made a rule (תקנה)
Held as a guarantee for a payment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the standard כתובה, which places a lien on all of the husband's property instead of requiring cash set aside.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
At first they would write
two hundred for a virgin and one hundred for a widow,
phrases.notes: These are amounts of זוז; a מנה is one hundred.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ מַזְקִינִין וְלֹא הָיוּ נוֹשְׂאִין נָשִׁים,
phrases.english: and men would grow old and not marry women,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח וְתִיקֵּן,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of שמעון בן שטח's rule, all of the husband's property is a guarantee for the כתובה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats רב יהודה's opening words: at first the sums were two hundred and one hundred, and men grew old without marrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: At first they wrote two hundred for a virgin and a מנה for a widow, and men grew old and did not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב יהודה. This sets up the next steps, where the ברייתא lists the fixes that were tried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same words as רב יהודה, so it backs up his history. It then gives more detail about the steps before שמעון בן שטח's final fix.

steps.title: First fix: keep the money at her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ruled that the כתובה money be kept in the wife's father's house. But an angry husband could easily tell her to go to her money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made a rule to keep it in her father's house. But there was still a problem: when he got angry at her, he would say, 'Go to your כתובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and describes the first fix that was tried, and the problem it caused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping the money safe at her father's house protected it. But the money was already sitting there for her, so divorce felt easy and cost the husband nothing new. An angry husband could just send her away.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the Sages) made a rule
And still (a problem remained)
Go to your כתובה (go away, your money is waiting)

phrases.english: They made a rule that they would keep it
in her father's house.
And still there was a problem: when he got angry at her,

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מַנִּיחִין אוֹתָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the first attempted fix.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כתובה money was kept at the wife's father's house, but this made divorce too easy.

steps.title: Second fix: keep the money in the husband's house
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ruled that the money be kept in her father-in-law's house. Rich women turned it into silver and gold baskets, and poor women turned it into a chamber pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made a rule to keep it in her father-in-law's house. Rich women made it into baskets of silver and gold. Poor women made it into a chamber pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the second fix. Keeping the money in the husband's home led to it being made into household objects. The ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the money was kept in the husband's home and not at her father's house. Wealthy women made theirs into silver and gold baskets, and poor women made theirs into a plain vessel. As the next step shows, this fix still did not stop an angry husband from sending her away, which prepares for the final fix of שמעון בן שטח.

keyTerms.meaning: Her father-in-law's house, the husband's family home
Baskets

phrases.english: They made a rule that they would keep it

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כתובה money was moved to the husband's home, where women made it into vessels, rich or plain.

steps.title: The final fix: all the husband's property backs the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Even with the money stored at the father-in-law's house, an angry husband could still easily send his wife away. שמעון בן שטח ruled that he writes: all my property is responsible for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, when he was angry at her, he would say to her: 'Take your כתובה and leave.' This went on until שמעון בן שטח came and made a new rule: the husband writes for her, 'All my property is responsible for her כתובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches the last stage of the story. The earlier fix still did not work, so שמעון בן שטח made the final rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every earlier fix kept the כתובה money set aside and ready, so divorce was quick and cheap for an angry husband. Now nothing is set aside. Instead all his property guarantees the כתובה, so to divorce her he would have to free up or sell his own assets, and that makes him stop and think.

keyTerms.meaning: And still: the problem had not gone away
Take your כתובה and leave: the angry husband's easy dismissal
Made a new rabbinic rule (תקנה)
Property that is responsible and acts as a guarantee for a debt

steps.whatToRemember: The full history of the כתובה: first the money was set aside, then it was kept in her father's house, then in her father-in-law's house. Each time divorce stayed too easy. In the end שמעון בן שטח ruled that all the husband's property guarantees the כתובה. This is the practice to this day.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a second opinion that argues with step 12. Step 12 (רב יהודה) gave the short version of the same final rule, and this ברייתא shows the full set of steps that led up to it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a כתובה is written as a lien on all of the husband's property and not as money set aside. The goal is to protect the wife by making divorce something a husband does not do lightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the fix in step 15 still failed, and brings the final rule that ends the series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband writes that all his property is responsible for the כתובה. No money is set aside.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמעון בן שטח's rule, that all the husband's property backs the כתובה, is the final form of the כתובה. It makes divorce hard enough that a husband will not do it in anger.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter האשה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line for finishing the chapter האשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter האשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the chapter that opened with 'האשה שנפלו לה נכסים.' It shows love for the learning and a hope to come back and learn it again.
